procedure: Project the validated independent source contract from the immutable successor audit; retain its full source evidence, conventions and ambiguities in the sealed output.

payload.source_label: A finite-volume unknown is the cell integral divided by cell volume rather than a point value

contract.statement: The selected passage defines the cell average of a solution field as its integral over a spatial grid cell divided by that cell's volume. Finite volume methods approximate these averages and update the approximate values using boundary fluxes computed from the available approximate averages [printed p. 5, Section 1.2, first paragraph]. The inherited context uses spatial dx integration at fixed time and permits vector-valued conserved densities and discontinuous solutions [printed p. 1, paragraph containing (1.1); printed p. 4, (1.10) and following paragraph; printed p. 5, continuation of Section 1.1.2]. The passage does not specify an arbitrary measure, analytic admissibility conditions, or behavior for zero-volume cells [printed p. 5, Section 1.2, defining clause].
assumptions: The domain is broken into grid cells in the finite volume description [printed p. 5, Section 1.2, “we break the domain into grid cells”].

The defining sentence presupposes that the relevant cell integral and division by cell volume are meaningful; it supplies no explicit integrability, measurability, or nonzero-volume hypotheses [printed p. 5, Section 1.2, cell-average defining clause].

The selected claim is a definition within a description of finite volume methods, rather than a numbered theorem with an explicit quantified hypothesis list [printed p. 5, Section 1.2, first paragraph].

Conservation laws supply the physical interpretation of the cell integral as a total conserved amount and of boundary fluxes as its mechanism of change [printed p. 4, Section 1.1.1, (1.10) and following paragraph].

Discontinuous solutions are part of the intended setting; classical differentiability of q is not a stated prerequisite for the cell-average definition [printed p. 5, continuation of Section 1.1.2 and opening of Section 1.2].

The constant-coefficient linear system on printed page 1 is introduced as a simplest case; the subsequent context also includes nonlinear conservation laws, so linearity and a fixed matrix A are not inherited requirements of the cell-average definition [printed p. 1, paragraph containing (1.1); printed p. 4, opening paragraph; printed p. 5, Section 1.2].
quantifiers: q is the solution field being averaged; the inherited one-dimensional presentation permits q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝᵐ, with spatial argument x and temporal argument t [printed p. 1, paragraph containing (1.1)].
A grid cell is a spatial piece of the domain; the definition applies to each such cell [printed p. 5, Section 1.2, “over each grid cell”].

Time is held fixed when forming a spatial cell integral; this is inherited from q(x,t) integrated against dx in (1.10), rather than explicitly rebound in the defining sentence [printed p. 4, (1.10); printed p. 5, Section 1.2].
